snippet.title: (Vlog) Claude Code Conference in SF | software updates & having fun !!
snippet.description:
went to anthropic’s first claude code conference and honestly this might be one of the most playful tech conferences i’ve ever been to 😭

there were tiny programmable cardputers, an 8-bit photobooth that turned us into pixel stickers, a claude-powered typewriter, maker stations, workshops, office hours, rooftop hangs, and somehow i ended up walking around the conference with a fish tamagotchi all day

also got to hear about some of anthropic’s newest releases around:

- multi-agent systems
- outcomes
- dreaming
- claude managed agents
- memory

my brain is still processing everything tbh but it genuinely made me excited to build weird little internet things again :))

🎀 let's be friends

tiktok: http://tiktok.com/@meshtimes

snippet.title: YouTube Was a Dating Site?! These Startup Pivots Changed Everything
snippet.description:
90% of startups fail — not because they run out of money, but because they build something nobody wants.

But what if failure… is actually the path to success? 💡

In this video, we dive deep into the power of the strategic pivot — and how billion-dollar companies like Instagram, Slack, Shopify, YouTube, and more completely changed direction and struck gold. 💰

Learn how Instagram went from a forgotten check-in app (Burbn) to 2 billion users, how Slack emerged from a failed online game, and how YouTube started as a video dating site… and ended up being the internet’s video king.

Whether you're a founder, entrepreneur, or just startup-curious, this breakdown will show you the exact moment these companies pivoted — and why it worked.

📖 Chapters
00:00 - Intro
00:49 - Instagram
02:50 - Slack
05:51 - YouTube
07:25 - Shopify
08:27 - Timing a Pivot
10:30 - How to Pivot
12:05 - Conclusion

📩 Need help with your career or building your business? 
Connect with me directly: https://www.operationskevin.com/

📣 Subscribe for more startup & business insights!
🔔 Turn on notifications so you don’t miss the next video!

👨🏻‍💻 About Operations Kevin:
I’m that odd person that's passionate about operations. I have the privilege of working on high-impact products and leading large-scale operations.

📍 How I Got Here:

- Graduated with a degree in aerospace engineering and started my career in aerospace manufacturing. 

- Worked on sweet products such as SpaceX’s Falcon 9 engine and Boeing’s LEAP engine.

- Transitioned into tech, joining Amazon as an operations manager. Led teams of 600+ at a last-mile delivery station. 

- Pivoted to program management and worked on Amazon’s machine learning-based hiring and recruitment efforts. Led a team of 5 program managers building software tools for large-scale hiring.

- Joined Apple as an iPhone ops program manager. Managed capacity & volume planning for iPhone SE, 11, 12, 13, and 14. 

- Drove strategic roadmap planning for future iPhone products, working with engineering, manufacturing, business ops, and finance teams.

Today: 
Left it all behind to pursue entrepreneurship. Currently scaling two businesses and consulting small businesses in industries that I’m passionate about. 

Join me for the ride.

📲 Follow me on social media:
Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/operationskevin/
Twitter/X: https://x.com/operationskevin

#startups #entrepreneurship #pivot

snippet.title: My Top 5 Content Agents (That Save Me 10+ Hours A Week)
snippet.description:
Work with me to scale your biz with AI agents: https://joinagentos.com/
Free resources: https://www.skool.com/promptwarrior

In this video I break down the 5 content automations I use to save 10+ hours every week and generate more views, without creating AI slop. Every automation starts from one original long-form source (my YouTube video) and repurposes it, so the content stays authentic.

Here's what I cover:

1. YouTube title & thumbnail ideas - using a vidIQ MCP connection plus a scraped library of channels in my niche to generate and score titles, then publish a draft to YouTube.

2. Newsletter writer - pulls my video transcript via the Tella MCP, writes the newsletter in my template, and drafts it straight into beehiiv via browser automation.

3. Long-form to short-form - a two-step skill with human feedback that suggests short-form topics, then writes scripts in my voice based on the long-form transcript.

4. Multi-platform scheduling - downloads the edited clips, writes captions from the scripts, and schedules everything across TikTok, Instagram, YouTube via Buffer plus Twitter and LinkedIn via Typefully.

5. Skool community poster - a browser automation that takes the latest YouTube video and posts it into my Skool community automatically.

If you want help implementing automations like these in your business, get in touch at https://joinagentos.com

I’m that odd person that's passionate about operations. I have the privilege of working on high-impact products and leading large-scale operations.

- Worked on sweet products such as SpaceX’s Falcon 9 engine and Boeing’s LEAP engine.

- Transitioned into tech, joining Amazon as an operations manager. Led teams of 600+ at a last-mile delivery station. 

- Pivoted to program management and worked on Amazon’s machine learning-based hiring and recruitment efforts. Led a team of 5 program managers building software tools for large-scale hiring.

- Joined Apple as an iPhone ops program manager. Managed capacity & volume planning for iPhone SE, 11, 12, 13, and 14. 

- Drove strategic roadmap planning for future iPhone products, working with engineering, manufacturing, business ops, and finance teams.

Today: 
Left it all behind to pursue entrepreneurship. Currently scaling two businesses and consulting small businesses in industries that I’m passionate about.

snippet.title: College kid built a $15K/month website… using these tools
snippet.description:
Maddox built duckmath.org from his dorm, scaled it from 5K to 150K daily active users in 4 months, and sold it for $120,000.

The wild part? The stack is dead simple:

Cloudflare for hosting + domains + static DB (free)
Supabase for backend, auth, user data ($20/mo)
PostHog for analytics + A/B testing ($50K in free startup credits)
Google AdSense for monetization (free)
Repurpose.io to auto cross-post ($30/mo)
React on the frontend, vibe-coded with AI
Discord (7K members) for community

He barely touched the code after AI hit. All the leverage went into volume: 3 TikTok accounts, 3 posts a day, 5 days a week.

snippet.title: GoHighLevel Review 2026: Is it Actually Worth it?
snippet.description:
In this GoHighLevel review, I answer whether the all-in-one CRM and SaaS platform is actually worth it, covering where it wins, where it's just okay, and where a specialty tool may be better.
✅ GoHighLevel (Exclusive 30-Day Free Trial): https://meticsmedia.com/gohighlevel-NSA

In this GoHighLevel review, I take an honest look at whether the all-in-one platform is actually worth it. GoHighLevel positions itself as a single CRM and SaaS platform that replaces 10+ separate tools, including your funnel builder, email and SMS marketing, calendar, automation engine, course platform, and reputation management, but the question most people are really asking is whether having everything in one place is worth more than picking the best tool in each category.

I'll walk you through GoHighLevel's main functional areas and break them into three buckets: where the platform clearly wins, where it's just okay, and where a specialty software might serve you better. You'll see how the CRM, automations, SMS marketing, and SaaS Mode white-label features stack up against dedicated tools like HubSpot, ActiveCampaign, ClickFunnels, Calendly, Kajabi, and Klaviyo. We'll also cover the pricing plans, the hidden usage costs people tend to miss, and the learning curve you should realistically expect before the platform starts paying off for your business.

By the end of the video, you'll know whether GoHighLevel is the right fit for your situation, whether you're running an agency, a service business, a coaching program, or any kind of small business.
